1 طَبَيْتُهُ عَنْهُ , (S, K,) aor. أَطْبِيهِ, inf. n. طَبْىٌ, (TA,) I turned him away, or back, from it, (Lth, S, K, TA,) namely, his opinion, and his affair, &c. (Lth, TA.) ―
-b2- And طَبَيْتُهُ إِلَيْهِ I called him to it; as also ↓ اِطَّبَيْتُهُ [in the CK erroneously written اَطْبَيْتُهُ]. (K, TA. See also art. طبو.) ―
-b3- And طَبَيْتُهُ I led him. (K, TA.) And thus Lh explains the ex. of this verb in the verse of Dhu-r-Rummeh cited voce ضَارِبٌ. (TA.) ＝
-A2- طَبِيَتْ, aor.
طَبَىَ , inf. n. طَبًى; (TA;) or طَبِيَتْ طَبًى شَدِيدًا; (K; [in the CK, erroneously, طَبْيًا;]) said of a she-camel, Her طُبْى [q. v.] was, or became, flaccid, flabby, or pendulous; (TA;) or very flaccid &c.; (K;) on the authority of Fr. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
